content.content:
1	# Templates
2	
3	Jujutsu supports a functional language to customize output of commands.
4	The language consists of literals, keywords, operators, functions, and
5	methods.
6	
7	A couple of `jj` commands accept a template via `-T`/`--template` option.
8	
9	## Keywords
10	
11	Keywords represent objects of different types; the types are described in
12	a follow-up section. In addition to context-specific keywords, the top-level
13	object can be referenced as `self`.
14	
15	### Commit keywords
16	
17	In `jj log` templates, all 0-argument methods of [the `Commit`
18	type](#commit-type) are available as keywords. For example, `commit_id` is
19	equivalent to `self.commit_id()`.
20	
21	### Operation keywords
22	
23	In `jj op log` templates, all 0-argument methods of [the `Operation`
24	type](#operation-type) are available as keywords. For example,
25	`current_operation` is equivalent to `self.current_operation()`.
26	
27	## Operators
28	
29	The following operators are supported. `x` and `y` below can be any expression.
30	
31	Operators are listed in order of binding power from strongest to weakest, e.g.
32	`x ++ y * z` is interpreted as `x ++ (y * z)` since `*` has stronger binding
33	power than `++`. Infix operators of the same binding power are parsed from left
34	to right, e.g. `x * y / z` is interpreted as `(x * y) / z`.
35	
36	As seen above, parentheses can be used to control evaluation order, e.g. `(x +
37	y) * z`.
38	
39	1. * `x.f()`: Method call.
40	   * `f(x)`: Function call.
41	
42	2. * `-x`: Negate integer value.
43	   * `!x`: Logical not.
44	
45	3. * `p:x`: String pattern or pattern alias named `p`.
46	
47	4. * `x * y`, `x / y`, `x % y`: Multiplication / division / remainder. Operands must
48	     be `Integer`s.
49	
50	5. * `x + y`, `x - y`: Addition / subtraction. Operands must be `Integer`s.
51	
52	6. * `x >= y`, `x > y`, `x <= y`, `x < y`: Greater than or equal / greater than /
53	     lesser than or equal / lesser than. Operands must be `Integer`s.
54	
55	7. * `x == y`, `x != y`: Equal / not equal. Operands must be either `Boolean`,
56	     `ByteString`, `Integer`, or `String`.
57	
58	8. * `x && y`: Logical and, short-circuiting.
59	
60	9. * `x || y`: Logical or, short-circuiting.
61	
62	10. * `x ++ y`: Concatenate `x` and `y` templates.
63	
64	## Global functions
65	
66	The following functions are defined.
67	
68	* `fill(width: Integer, content: Template) -> Template`: Fill lines at
69	  the given `width`.
70	* `indent(prefix: Template, content: Template) -> Template`: Indent
71	  non-empty lines by the given `prefix`.
72	* `pad_start(width: Integer, content: Template, [fill_char: Template])`: Pad (or
73	  right-justify) content by adding leading fill characters. The `content`
74	  shouldn't have newline character.
75	* `pad_end(width: Integer, content: Template, [fill_char: Template])`: Pad (or
76	  left-justify) content by adding trailing fill characters. The `content`
77	  shouldn't have newline character.
78	* `pad_centered(width: Integer, content: Template, [fill_char: Template])`: Pad
79	  content by adding both leading and trailing fill characters. If an odd number
80	  of fill characters are needed, the trailing fill will be one longer than the
81	  leading fill. The `content` shouldn't have newline characters.
82	* `truncate_start(width: Integer, content: Template, [ellipsis: Template])`:
83	  Truncate `content` by removing leading characters. The `content` shouldn't
84	  have newline character. If `ellipsis` is provided and `content` was truncated,
85	  prepend the `ellipsis` to the result.
86	* `truncate_end(width: Integer, content: Template, [ellipsis: Template])`:
87	  Truncate `content` by removing trailing characters. The `content` shouldn't
88	  have newline character. If `ellipsis` is provided and `content` was truncated,
89	  append the `ellipsis` to the result.
90	* `hash(content: Stringify) -> String`:
91	  Hash the input and return a hexadecimal string representation of the digest.
92	* `label(label: Stringify, content: Template) -> Template`: Apply a custom
93	  [color label](#color-labels) to the content. The `label` is evaluated as a
94	  space-separated string.
95	* `hyperlink(url: Stringify, text: Template, [fallback: Template]) -> Template`:
96	  Render `text` as a hyperlink to `url` using [OSC 8 escape sequences](https://github.com/Alhadis/OSC8-Adoption)
97	  when outputting with color enabled. Otherwise, renders `fallback` instead,
98	  which defaults to `text`. Use `--color=always` to force hyperlinks when piping
99	  output to a terminal emulator that supports OSC 8.
100	* `raw_escape_sequence(content: Template) -> Template`: Preserves any escape
101	  sequences in `content` (i.e., bypasses sanitization) and strips labels.
102	  Note: This function is intended for escape sequences and as such, its output
103	  is expected to be invisible / of no display width. Outputting content with
104	  nonzero display width may break wrapping, indentation etc.
105	* `replace(pattern: StringPattern, content: Template, replacement: |RegexCaptures| -> Template) -> Template`:
106	  Replace every match of `pattern` in `content` by formatting the `replacement`
107	  lambda for each match.
108	
109	  This is similar to [`String.replace()`](#string-type), but operates on
110	  `Template` content and preserves formatting of the parts of `content` that are
111	  not replaced. The replacement itself is newly formatted template content.
112	
113	  The lambda argument is a [`RegexCaptures`](#regexcaptures-type) value for the
114	  current match. Use `.get(index)` to access capture groups by index, `.name(name)`
115	  to access named capture groups, and `.len()` to get the number of captures
116	  including capture group 0 for the full match.
117	* `stringify(content: Stringify) -> String`: Format `content` to string. This
118	  effectively removes color labels.
119	* `json(value: Serialize) -> String`: Serialize `value` in JSON format.
120	* `if(condition: Boolean, then: Any, [else: Any]) -> Any`:
121	  Conditionally evaluates to `then` / `else` content.
122	* `coalesce(content: Template...) -> Template`: Returns the first **non-empty**
123	  content.
124	* `concat(content: Template...) -> Template`:
125	  Same as `content_1 ++ ... ++ content_n`.
126	* `join(separator: Template, content: Template...) -> Template`: Insert
127	  `separator` between `content`s.
128	* `separate(separator: Template, content: Template...) -> Template`: Insert
129	  `separator` between **non-empty** `content`s.
130	* `surround(prefix: Template, suffix: Template, content: Template) -> Template`:
131	  Surround **non-empty** content with texts such as parentheses.
132	* `config(name: Stringify) -> Option<ConfigValue>`: Look up configuration
133	   value by `name`.
134	* `git_web_url([remote: String]) -> String`: Best-effort conversion of a git
135	  remote URL to an HTTPS web URL. Defaults to the "origin" remote. Returns an
136	  empty string on failure. SSH host alias resolution is currently unsupported.
137	
138	## Types
139	
140	### `AnnotationLine` type
141	
142	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: no, `Template`: no_
143	
144	The following methods are defined.
145	
146	* `.commit() -> Commit`: Commit responsible for changing the relevant line.
147	* `.content() -> ByteString`: Line content including newline character.
148	* `.line_number() -> Integer`: 1-based line number.
149	* `.original_line_number() -> Integer`: 1-based line number in the original commit.
150	* `.first_line_in_hunk() -> Boolean`: False when the directly preceding line
151	  references the same commit.
152	
153	### `Any` type
154	
155	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: maybe, `Template`: maybe_
156	
157	All types can be implicitly converted to `Any`. No methods are defined.
158	
159	### `AnyList` type
160	
161	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: maybe, `Template`: maybe_
162	
163	The following methods are defined.
164	
165	* `.join(separator: Template) -> Template`: Concatenate elements with
166	  the given `separator`.
167	
168	### `Boolean` type
169	
170	_Conversion: `Boolean`: yes, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
171	
172	No methods are defined. Can be constructed with `false` or `true` literal.
173	
174	### `ByteString` type
175	
176	_Conversion: `Boolean`: yes, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
177	
178	A byte string, whose encoding is considered ASCII-compatible (e.g. UTF-8), but
179	isn't guaranteed. This can be implicitly converted to `Boolean`. The following
180	methods are defined.
181	
182	* `.len() -> Integer`: Length in bytes.
183	* `.contains(needle: ByteStringify) -> Boolean`: Whether the string contains the
184	  provided stringifiable value as a substring.
185	* `.match(needle: StringPattern) -> ByteString`: Extract the first matching part
186	  of the string for the given pattern.
187	
188	  An empty string is returned if there is no match.
189	* `.starts_with(needle: ByteStringify) -> Boolean`: Whether `needle` is a
190	  prefix of the string.
191	* `.ends_with(needle: ByteStringify) -> Boolean`: Whether `needle` is a suffix
192	  of the string.
193	* `.remove_prefix(needle: ByteStringify) -> ByteString`: Remove the passed
194	  prefix, if present.
195	* `.remove_suffix(needle: ByteStringify) -> ByteString`: Remove the passed
196	  suffix, if present.
197	* `.trim() -> ByteString`: Remove leading and trailing ASCII whitespace.
198	* `.trim_start() -> ByteString`: Remove leading ASCII whitespace.
199	* `.trim_end() -> ByteString`: Remove trailing ASCII whitespace.
200	* `.substr(start: Integer, [end: Integer]) -> ByteString`: Extract substring.
201	  Indices are 0-based and `end` is exclusive. Negative values count from the end
202	  of the string, with `-1` being the last byte. If `end` is not given, returns
203	  from `start` to the end of the string.
204	* `.first_line() -> ByteString`
205	* `.lines() -> List<ByteString>`: Split into lines excluding newline characters.
206	* `.split(separator: StringPattern, [limit: Integer]) -> List<ByteString>`:
207	  Split into substrings by the given `separator` pattern. If `limit` is
208	  specified, it determines the maximum number of elements in the result, with
209	  the remainder of the string returned as the final element. A `limit` of 0
210	  returns an empty list.
211	* `.replace(pattern: StringPattern, replacement: ByteStringify, [limit:
212	  Integer]) -> ByteString`: Replace occurrences of the given `pattern` with the
213	  `replacement` string.
214	
215	  By default, all occurrences are replaced. If `limit` is specified, at most
216	  that many occurrences are replaced.
217	
218	  Supports capture groups in patterns using `$0` (entire match), `$1`, `$2` etc.
219	* `.upper() -> ByteString`: Map each ASCII character to upper case.
220	* `.lower() -> ByteString`: Map each ASCII character to lower case.
221	
222	### `ByteStringify` type
223	
224	An expression that can be converted to a `ByteString`.
225	
226	A `String` can be converted to a `ByteString` losslessly. Any types that can be
227	converted to `Template` can also be `ByteStringify`. Unlike `Template`, color
228	labels are stripped.
229	
230	### `ChangeId` type
231	
232	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
233	
234	The following methods are defined.
235	
236	* `.normal_hex() -> String`: Normal hex representation (0-9a-f) instead of the
237	  canonical "reversed" (z-k) representation.
238	* `.short([len: Integer]) -> String`
239	* `.shortest([min_len: Integer]) -> ShortestIdPrefix`: Shortest unique prefix.
240	
241	### `Commit` type
242	
243	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: no_
244	
245	This type cannot be printed. The following methods are defined.
246	
247	* `.description() -> String`: Usually ends with a trailing `\n`, if non-blank.
248	* `.trailers() -> List<Trailer>`: The trailers at the end of the commit
249	  description that are formatted as `<key>: <value>`. These are returned in the
250	  same order as they appear in the description, and there may be multiple
251	  `Trailer`s with the same key.
252	* `.change_id() -> ChangeId`
253	* `.commit_id() -> CommitId`
254	* `.parents() -> List<Commit>`
255	* `.author() -> Signature`
256	* `.committer() -> Signature`
257	* `.signature() -> Option<CryptographicSignature>`: Cryptographic signature if
258	  the commit was signed.
259	* `.mine() -> Boolean`: Commits where the author's email matches the email of
260	  the current user.
261	* `.working_copies() -> List<WorkspaceRef>`: For multi-workspace repositories,
262	  returns a list of workspace references for each workspace whose working-copy
263	  commit matches the current commit.
264	* `.current_working_copy() -> Boolean`: True for the working-copy commit of the
265	  current workspace.
266	* `.bookmarks() -> List<CommitRef>`: Local and remote bookmarks pointing to the
267	  commit. A tracked remote bookmark will be included only if its target is
268	  different from the local one.
269	* `.local_bookmarks() -> List<CommitRef>`: All local bookmarks pointing to the
270	  commit.
271	* `.remote_bookmarks() -> List<CommitRef>`: All remote bookmarks pointing to the
272	  commit.
273	* `.tags() -> List<CommitRef>`: Local and remote tags pointing to the commit. A
274	  tracked remote tag will be included only if its target is different from the
275	  local one.
276	* `.local_tags() -> List<CommitRef>`: All local tags pointing to the commit.
277	* `.remote_tags() -> List<CommitRef>`: All remote tags pointing to the commit.
278	* `.divergent() -> Boolean`: True if the commit's change ID corresponds to multiple
279	  visible commits.
280	* `.hidden() -> Boolean`: True if the commit is not visible (a.k.a. abandoned).
281	* `.change_offset() -> Option<Integer>`: The [change offset](glossary.md#change-offset)
282	  of this commit. May not be available for some commits.
283	* `.immutable() -> Boolean`: True if the commit is included in [the set of
284	  immutable commits](config.md#set-of-immutable-commits).
285	* `.contained_in(revset: StringLiteral) -> Boolean`: True if the commit is included in
286	  [the provided revset](revsets.md).
287	* `.conflict() -> Boolean`: True if the commit contains merge conflicts.
288	* `.empty() -> Boolean`: True if the commit modifies no files.
289	* `.diff([files: StringLiteral]) -> TreeDiff`: Changes from the parents within [the
290	  `files` expression](filesets.md). All files are compared by default, but it is
291	  likely to change in future version to respect the command line path arguments.
292	* `.files([files: StringLiteral]) -> List<TreeEntry>`: Files that exist in this commit,
293	  matching [the `files` expression](filesets.md). Use `.diff().files()` to list
294	  changed files.
295	* `.conflicted_files() -> List<TreeEntry>`: Conflicted files in this commit.
296	* `.root() -> Boolean`: True if the commit is the root commit.
297	
298	### `CommitEvolutionEntry` type
299	
300	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: no_
301	
302	This type cannot be printed. The following methods are defined.
303	
304	* `.commit() -> Commit`: New commit.
305	* `.operation() -> Operation`: Operation where the commit was created or
306	  rewritten.
307	* `.predecessors() -> List<Commit>`: Predecessor commits of this entry.
308	* `.inter_diff([files: StringLiteral]) -> TreeDiff`: Changes between this commit and its
309	  predecessor version(s), rebased onto the parents of this commit to avoid unrelated
310	  changes (similar to `jj evolog -p`).
311	
312	### `CommitId` type
313	
314	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
315	
316	The following methods are defined.
317	
318	* `.short([len: Integer]) -> String`
319	* `.shortest([min_len: Integer]) -> ShortestIdPrefix`: Shortest unique prefix.
320	
321	### `CommitRef` type
322	
323	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
324	
325	The following methods are defined.
326	
327	* `.name() -> RefSymbol`: Local bookmark or tag name.
328	* `.remote() -> Option<RefSymbol>`: Remote name if this is a remote ref.
329	* `.present() -> Boolean`: True if the ref points to any commit.
330	* `.conflict() -> Boolean`: True if [the bookmark or tag is
331	  conflicted](bookmarks.md#conflicts).
332	* `.normal_target() -> Option<Commit>`: Target commit if the ref is not
333	  conflicted and points to a commit.
334	* `.removed_targets() -> List<Commit>`: Old target commits if conflicted.
335	* `.added_targets() -> List<Commit>`: New target commits. The list usually
336	  contains one "normal" target.
337	* `.tracked() -> Boolean`: True if the ref is tracked by a local ref. The local
338	  ref might have been deleted (but not pushed yet.)
339	* `.tracking_present() -> Boolean`: True if the ref is tracked by a local ref,
340	    and if the local ref points to any commit.
341	* `.tracking_ahead_count() -> SizeHint`: Number of commits ahead of the tracking
342	  local ref.
343	* `.tracking_behind_count() -> SizeHint`: Number of commits behind of the
344	  tracking local ref.
345	* `.synced() -> Boolean`: For a local bookmark, true if synced with all tracked
346	  remotes. For a remote bookmark, true if synced with the tracking local
347	  bookmark.
348	
349	### `ConfigValue` type
350	
351	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: yes, `Template`: yes_
352	
353	This type can be printed in TOML syntax. The following methods are defined.
354	
355	* `.as_boolean() -> Boolean`: Extract boolean.
356	* `.as_integer() -> Integer`: Extract integer.
357	* `.as_string() -> String`: Extract string. This does not convert non-string
358	  value (e.g. integer) to string.
359	* `.as_string_list() -> List<String>`: Extract list of strings.
360	
361	### `CryptographicSignature` type
362	
363	_Conversion: `Boolean`: no, `Serialize`: no, `Template`: no_
364	
365	The following methods are defined.
366	
367	* `.status() -> String`: The signature's status (`"good"`, `"bad"`, `"unknown"`,
368	  `"invalid"`).
369	* `.key() -> String`: The signature's key id representation (for GPG and SSH,
370	  this is the public key fingerprint).

372	  formatted primary user ID; for SSH, this is the principal).

377	    the performance cost of verifying the signature (for example shelling out
378	    to `gpg` or `ssh-keygen`). Though consecutive calls will be faster, because
379	    the backend caches the verification result.

382	
383	    As opposed to calling any of `.status()`, `.key()`, or `.display()`,
384	    checking for signature presence through boolean coercion is fast:

649	### `StringLiteral` type
650	
651	A string literal known at parse time. Unlike `Stringify`, this cannot be a
652	dynamic expression - it must be a literal value like `"main"` or `"format"`.
653	
654	String literals must be surrounded by single or double quotes (`'` or `"`).
655	A double-quoted string literal supports the following escape sequences:
656	
657	* `\"`: double quote
658	* `\\`: backslash
659	* `\t`: horizontal tab
660	* `\r`: carriage return
661	* `\n`: new line
662	* `\0`: null
663	* `\e`: escape (i.e., `\x1b`)
664	* `\xHH`: byte with hex value `HH`
665	
666	Other escape sequences are not supported. Any UTF-8 characters are allowed
667	inside a string literal, with two exceptions: unescaped `"`-s and uses of `\`
668	that don't form a valid escape sequence.
669	
670	A single-quoted string literal has no escape syntax. `'` can't be expressed
671	inside a single-quoted string literal.
672	
673	String literals have their own type so that the value can be validated at parse
674	time. For example, `contained_in(revset)` requires a literal so the revset can
675	be parsed and checked before the template is evaluated.

793	## Color labels
794	
795	You can [customize the output colors][config-colors] by using color labels. `jj`
796	adds some labels automatically; they can also be added manually.
797	
798	Template fragments are usually **automatically** labeled with the command name,
799	the context (or the top-level object), and the method names. For example, the
800	following template is labeled as `op_log operation id short` automatically:
801	
802	```sh
803	jj op log -T 'self.id().short()'
804	```
805	
806	The exact names of such labels are often straightforward, but are not currently
807	documented. You can discover the actual label names used with the
808	`--color=debug` option, e.g.
809	
810	```sh
811	jj op log -T 'self.id().short()' --color=debug
812	```
813	
814	Additionally, you can **manually** insert arbitrary labels using the
815	`label(label, content)` function. For example,
816	
817	```sh
818	jj op log -T '"ID: " ++ self.id().short().substr(0, 1) ++ label("id short", "<redacted>")'
819	```
820	
821	will print "ID:" in the default style, and the string `<redacted>` in the same
822	style as the first character of the id. It would also be fine to use an
823	arbitrary template instead of the string `"<redacted>"`, possibly including
824	nested invocations of `label()`.
825	
826	You are free to use custom label names as well. This will only have a visible
827	effect if you also [customize their colors][config-colors] explicitly.
828	
829	[config-colors]: config.md#custom-colors-and-styles
830	
831	## Configuration
832	
833	The default templates and aliases() are defined in the `[templates]` and
834	`[template-aliases]` sections of the config respectively. The exact definitions
835	can be seen in the [`cli/src/config/templates.toml`][1] file in jj's source
836	tree.
837	
838	[1]: https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/main/cli/src/config/templates.toml
839	
840	<!--- TODO: Find a way to embed the default config files in the docs -->
841	
842	New keywords, functions, and `<name>:<value>` patterns can be defined as
843	aliases, by using any combination of the predefined keywords/functions and other
844	aliases.
845	
846	Alias functions can be overloaded by the number of parameters. However, builtin
847	functions will be shadowed by name, and can't co-exist with aliases.
848	
849	For example:
850	
851	```toml
852	[template-aliases]
853	'commit_change_ids' = '''
854	concat(
855	  format_field("Commit ID", commit_id),
856	  format_field("Change ID", change_id),
857	)
858	'''
859	'format_field(key, value)' = 'key ++ ": " ++ value ++ "\n"'
860	'json:x' = 'json(x) ++ "\n"'
861	```
862	
863	## Examples
864	
865	Get short commit IDs of the working-copy parents:
866	
867	```sh
868	jj log -G -r @ -T 'parents.map(|c| c.commit_id().short()).join(",")'
869	```
870	
871	Show machine-readable list of full commit and change IDs:
872	
873	```sh
874	jj log -G -T 'commit_id ++ " " ++ change_id ++ "\n"'
875	```
876	
877	Print the description of the current commit, defaulting to `(no description set)`:
878	
879	```sh
880	jj log -G -r @ -T 'coalesce(description, "(no description set)\n")'
881	```

1	# Configuration

3	These are the config settings available to jj/Jujutsu.
4	
5	## Config files and TOML
6	
7	`jj` loads several types of config settings:
8	
9	- The built-in settings. These cannot be edited. They can be viewed in the
10	  [`cli/src/config/`] directory in `jj`'s source repo.
11	
12	- The user settings. These can be edited with `jj config edit --user`. User
13	  settings are located in [the user config files], which can be found with
14	  `jj config path --user`.
15	
16	- The repo settings. These can be edited with `jj config edit --repo`, or found
17	  with `jj config path --repo`. For security reasons, they are not located
18	  inside the repo.
19	
20	- The workspace settings. These can be edited with `jj config edit --workspace`,
21	  or found with `jj config path --workspace`. For security reasons, they are not
22	  located inside the workspace.
23	
24	- Settings [specified on the command-line].
25	
26	These are listed in the order they are loaded; the settings from earlier items
27	in the list are overridden by the settings from later items if they disagree.
28	Every type of config except for the built-in settings is optional.

31	reference at the top of your TOML config files. See [JSON Schema Support] for

45	[TOML site]: https://toml.io/en/
46	
47	### Dotted style and headings
48	
49	In TOML, anything under a heading can be dotted instead. For example,
50	`user.name = "YOUR NAME"` is equivalent to:
51	
52	```toml
53	[user]
54	name = "YOUR NAME"
55	```
56	
57	For future reference, here are a couple of more complicated examples,
58	
59	```toml
60	# Dotted style
61	template-aliases."format_short_id(id)" = "id.shortest(12)"
62	colors."commit_id prefix".bold = true
63	
64	# is equivalent to:
65	[template-aliases]
66	"format_short_id(id)" = "id.shortest(12)"
67	
68	[colors]
69	"commit_id prefix" = { bold = true }
70	```
71	
72	The docs below refer to keys in text using dotted notation, but example blocks
73	will use heading notation to be unambiguous. If you are confident with TOML then
74	use whichever suits you in your config. If you mix dotted keys and headings,
75	**you must put the dotted keys before the first heading**.
76	
77	### Escapes in strings
78	
79	There are two (or four) types of [strings in TOML]: basic and literal, with
80	multi-line versions of each. Basic strings use double quotes (`"`) and support
81	escape sequences, such as `"\n"`, `"\""`, `"\\"`, etc. Literal strings use
82	single quotes (`'`) and do not support escape sequences. Using 3 double quotes
83	or 3 single quotes to wrap a string makes it multi-line, and then you can use an
84	unescaped double quote or single quote respectively without ending the string.
85	
86	A string in your config may be interpreted twice, first by the TOML parser and
87	then by a Jujutsu parser. To avoid putting strings in your config that the TOML
88	parser processes before it gets to the Jujutsu parser, you may want to use
89	literal strings or literal multi-line strings in your `config.toml` files. For
90	example:
91	
92	```toml
93	[template-aliases]
94	# basic_template = "'hello' ++ \"\n\""
95	literal_template = '"hello" ++ "\n"'
96	```
97	
98	`basic_template` is actually equivalent to this string:
99	
100	```
101	'hello' ++ "
102	"
103	```
104	
105	because the TOML parser interprets the `\n` character as part of the string.
106	This causes the Jujutsu parser to receive a different string than what you
107	literally see in the TOML file, which may result in seemingly confusing parse
108	error messages (such as referencing a line that you think shouldn't exist).
109	
110	On the other hand, `literal_template` is equivalent to:
111	
112	```
113	"hello" ++ "\n"
114	```
115	
116	because the TOML parser does not escape anything in the literal string.
117	
118	The same rules of basic and literal strings apply to custom Jujutsu languages:
119	double quotes (`"`) allow escapes whereas single quotes (`'`) do not. So
120	`template-aliases.my_template = "'hello\\n'"` would probably not be what you
121	want.
122	
123	[strings in TOML]: https://toml.io/en/latest#string
124	
125	## User settings
126	
127	```toml
128	[user]
129	name = "YOUR NAME"
130	email = "YOUR_EMAIL@example.com"
131	```
132	
133	Don't forget to change these to your own details!
134	
135	## UI settings
136	
137	### Colorizing output
138	
139	Possible values are `always`, `never`, `debug` and `auto` (default: `auto`).
140	`auto` will use color only when writing to a terminal. `debug` will print the
141	active labels alongside the regular colorized output.
142	
143	This setting overrides the `NO_COLOR` environment variable (if set).
144	
145	```toml
146	[ui]
147	color = "never" # Turn off color
148	```
